title: Install and operate Bazaar
summary: Install Bazaar and its provider, initialize an empty private string database, or check and recover program selection without changing stored versions.

consumers.statement: Local programs use the in-process bazaar::api Rust API. People and authorized agents use the Bazaar CLI.

preconditions.statement: Program installation requires an authorized supplied Bazaar program/provider candidate; program-only inspection or recovery does not require initialized data. Init requires an absolute private path and absent, empty, or compatible state and can create missing paths. Doctor requires initialized schema-one state.

data_semantics.statement: Initialization creates only the versions table, its constraints and database identity. It creates no string versions. Program installation does not select or interpret content.

identity_and_units.statement: Opaque UUID release IDs select retained program archives. Executable files run at fixed actual paths beneath Bazaar/install/runtime. Database schema, release version and string versions are independent.

access.statement: The current user's filesystem permissions protect state. Rust readers open SQLite read-only and expose no writes. CLI dispatch separately attempts metadata-only Chancery usage recording; direct API reads do not.

operational_limits.statement: The procedure stops for foreign or unsupported state, invalid or nonprivate paths, foreign selectors, changed release bytes, stale expected selection, or failed configure or verification. Content updates require separate authorization. Detailed state limits are owned by the required bazaar.installation feature.

Deploy accepts one bounded schema-two recipe request on stdin. The product command owns its setup; the shared executor uses process exit status only. Deployment runs no application execution probe, native-signature audit, maintenance hold, drain, or automatic rollback.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Bazaar accepts database schema one. New releases use cell-install-v4; retained earlier formats remain readable. Foreign, nonempty uninitialized, and unsupported databases are refused without migration. Program rollback does not restore older data.

reliances.statement: Core state operations use local SQLite and files. No external service, model, or installed catalog is a runtime dependency.

The Cell manifest executor runs declared instructions in product order and checks their exit status. Bazaar owns file selection and default-state initialization. The executor imposes no application readiness, maintenance, or recovery policy.

inputs.statement: The manifest executor supplies the schema-two recipe request. Bazaar accepts no deployment settings. Direct installation takes absolute --binary and --bundle paths and optional --home and --expected-current. CLI --database selects an explicit private database.

outputs.statement: The procedure reports selected program/provider checks and schema-one initialization or doctor results without string content. Completion requires the relevant program identity or database checks; coordinated deployment performs setup without a separate verification gate. Documentation discovery alone does not establish either.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Installation reads selectors and metadata without integrity checks. Doctor checks local database identity and SQLite quick_check; it establishes no future availability or content correctness.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Shared cell-install-v4 file transactions select matching programs and provider. Init preserves existing versions and can complete interrupted empty initialization. Compatible program upgrade and recovery preserve the separate database. No daemon or scheduler is installed.

use_when: Installing or recovering Bazaar programs, initializing empty state, or checking database integrity.
do_not_use_when: Reading or editing an individual string, migrating caller configurations, or executing agents.
outcome: Selected Bazaar programs and compatible initialized state, or the requested read-only check.
effects: Installation changes owned program/provider selectors. The Bazaar deployment recipe initializes an absent database. Existing content is preserved; no version is appended.
authority: Bazaar owns its program selection and private database. The Cell manifest executor owns declared instruction ordering and exit-status tracking.
success: For a program operation, owned programs and provider selectors select the supplied release. For a database operation, selected schema-one identity and integrity checks pass. Coordinated deployment performs setup without an additional verification gate.
failure_and_recovery: Refuse foreign selectors, stale expected selections and unsupported state. Retained-release program recovery leaves database history intact. After an interrupted initialization, repeat init only against the same empty or compatible state.
privacy: The default database is ~/.local/share/bazaar/bazaar.sqlite3. State stays outside source and release files.
does_not_authorize: Writing string content, migrating callers, deleting or restoring data, executing a model, or activating a schedule.
steps: Select the intended operation, authorization, absolute private database, and supplied candidate or exact retained release.

Submit the selected committed source through CI and Telete with explicit Bazaar deployment selection, then verify the retained manager job outcome. Product installer APIs remain underlying setup and explicit recovery interfaces.
Initialize only intended empty or compatible state, then run doctor and register the installed command inventory separately.

Read program selection metadata; run database doctor only for a separate diagnostic request. When the Chancery reader is installed, inspect overview/show/resolve separately; those views do not establish runtime readiness.
For program recovery select an exact owned compatible release, preserve database history, and read installation metadata.
checkpoints: The selected database and installation changes are authorized; content updates and caller migration remain separate.
For state operations, existing parent and database paths are regular and private and data is absent, empty, or compatible as required. Program candidates and selectors have established ownership.
The retained manager job identifies the intended Bazaar deployment and its result; explicit configure and verification operations succeed when they form part of the authorized endpoint.

Program inspection reads selectors and retained metadata and relevant database checks confirm schema-one identity and integrity. Coordinated deployment performs setup without an additional verification gate.
Program recovery retains all string versions.
adaptation: Use the global --database option for an explicit private database; coordinated deployment configures only the default.
Use the installer --home and --expected-current guards when the installation home or expected selection must be explicit.
Use read-only inspect and doctor when no state or selection change is intended.
Skip catalog reading when the Chancery executable is absent; sealed program/provider checks and core state operations work independently.
stop_when: The selected change lacks authorization or would append content, migrate callers, delete history, or execute an agent outside this operation.

For a database operation, existing parent/database paths are not absolute, regular, and private, a symlink is present, or state is foreign, unsupported, or absent when the check requires initialized state.
A selector is foreign, release bytes changed, expected selection is stale, or installation evidence remains unresolved.
Required setup fails, or a separately requested database diagnostic fails.
